first_impression.reaction: The intro reads like a brochure, but the key takeaways give me a dated Smartraveller rating and the registration point straight away, so I kept going. I went to the FAQ first. It's short but direct, then I went back up for the detail on speeches, mats and the legal bit.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Exercise normal safety precautions" in Samoa, and an overseas marriage can't be registered in Australia, though it is usually recognised.
journey.reaction: Dated and specific, right at the top. That's the kind of line I can check in thirty seconds.

journey.section: Samoan wedding traditions start with family
journey.quote: There is no single script for a traditional Samoan wedding.
journey.reaction: Fair. Better than pretending there's one right way and then selling me a package built around it.

journey.section: 2. The families meet: orators and formal speeches
journey.quote: Couples often ask who pays for a Samoan wedding. In many families, the cost and the work are shared across the aiga on both sides, with relatives contributing food, gifts and time.
journey.reaction: Okay, but that's the family side. If the aiga covers food and gifts, what's left for a planner to charge for? That's the question I actually have, and it isn't answered.

journey.section: 3. Fine mats ('ie toga) and gifts between families
journey.quote: Give the presentation unhurried time and a sheltered, dignified space, and agree handling, display and transport with the family, not with suppliers.
journey.reaction: Practical, and it tells me to keep suppliers out of something. That's not a business trying to upsell me on every part of the day.

journey.quote: For a real celebration from our pages, see [Mercy and Chanel's traditional Samoan wedding](/a-traditional-samoan-wedding-celebration).
journey.reaction: A real wedding is good. I'll click it, but what I want is what it cost and what the planner actually did. If that page is just photos, it doesn't help me much.

journey.section: 8. The wedding feast and the umu
journey.quote: For a destination wedding, ask early whether your venue allows an umu on the grounds, or whether the family will cook off site and bring the food in.
journey.reaction: Useful. That's a real catch with resorts and it's the sort of thing I'd want spelled out before signing anything.

journey.quote: Sunday activities are extremely limited and alcohol can't be sold, though hotels and resorts operate normally; be respectful passing through villages.
journey.reaction: Good. Downsides stated plainly, including the same-sex recognition point. A wedding company that tells you the limitations gets more credit from me.

journey.quote: Before you book, put these questions to Samoa's Births, Deaths and Marriages registry and the Australian High Commission in Apia:
journey.reaction: A clear checklist of what to ask and who to ask. I'd rather have the answers, but at least I know the questions and the offices. Workable.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for venue, travel, vendors and guest rooms, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, with the fee and inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee and inclusions in writing before I commit is what I need to see. It still doesn't say whether they take a cut from the venue or vendors they put me onto.

journey.section: Planning a Samoan wedding with us
journey.quote: When you are ready to talk through dates, islands or a wedding at home, a Wedded Advisor is happy to start the conversation.
journey.reaction: Soft close. Fine, but tell me what that first call covers and whether it costs anything.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues and vendors?
What does the Wedded Advisor fee cover and how is it calculated?
Have they planned a wedding in Samoa itself, and is there a real example with the actual budget?
Is the first conversation with a Wedded Advisor free, and what does it cover?
If the families handle food, gifts and the ceremony, which parts would a planner actually take on?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Samoan Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Clickbait headline, and the article is better than it. Title was set by the person, so noted only.

turn_offs_found.quote: When you are ready to talk through dates, islands or a wedding at home, a Wedded Advisor is happy to start the conversation.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Happy to start the conversation' is a soft sell. Say what the call is and whether it costs anything.

would_share_with: My partner, for the Smartraveller and legal steps section
Her parents or elders, to check which parts their family actually keeps and who would speak for each side

cta_reaction.quote: A Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for venue, travel, vendors and guest rooms, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, with the fee and inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the evidence, not before, and the written fee line is the right signal. I'd still look for a fees or commissions page before handing over my details.

top_3_changes: Say, even in one line, whether the Wedded Advisor takes commissions or mark-ups from suppliers (business detail deferred, so nice-to-have).
Swap 'happy to start the conversation' for what the first call covers and whether it's free.
After 'who pays for a Samoan wedding', add a line on what a planner handles versus what the families usually take on, so I can see what the fee would buy.
